purpose: Naftifine is used to treat fungal skin infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It helps clear up the rash, itching, and irritation caused by these infections. It is only used on the skin, not taken by mouth.
how_it_works: Naftifine works by blocking a key step that fungi need to build their outer protective layer called the cell membrane. Without this layer, the fungus cannot survive and eventually dies off. This stops the infection from spreading and allows your skin to heal.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or redness at the spot where you apply it. Some people notice dryness, itching, or a rash at the application site. These effects are usually mild and go away as your skin gets used to the medicine.
warnings: Do not use this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or inside the nose. If your skin gets very irritated, swollen, or you develop a rash that spreads, stop using it and contact your doctor. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this product. Keep using it for the full prescribed time even if your skin looks better, so the infection does not come back.
typical_dosing: For the cream (1% or 2%), it is usually applied to the affected area once a day. For the gel (1%), it is typically applied twice a day, morning and evening. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions. Treatment usually lasts 2 to 4 weeks depending on the type of infection.
